Set the test priority that rating produces and record the reasoning for it.
List the systems held out of scope, with the reason for each exclusion.

title.en: Document the resilience testing programme and how it sits within the ICT risk management framework

description.en: Produce the programme document: what the testing sets out to establish, the test types it uses, how the scope register's risk ratings drive what is tested and in what order, the requirement that tests are performed by independent parties, how findings are prioritised and remediated, and the point at which results feed back into the ICT risk management framework. Name the role accountable for the programme. Attach the issued programme with its version number and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: The issued digital operational resilience testing programme, versioned and dated, covering test types, risk-based prioritisation, tester independence, remediation and the link to the ICT risk management framework

title.en: Build the test plan and schedule assigning each in-scope system a test type and a test window

description.en: Turn the programme into a dated plan. For every entry in the scope register, record the test type it receives, the window within the programme cycle in which it will be tested, the party that will perform it, and the access or environment the test depends on. Show the coverage of critical systems across the cycle explicitly, so a system the plan never reaches is visible while the cycle can still be changed rather than discovered when it ends. Attach the test plan and schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Test plan and schedule: each in-scope system with its test type, test window, performing party, access dependencies, and the coverage view across the programme cycle

title.en: Confirm the independence of the party performing each test before the engagement starts

description.en: Before a test begins, check and record that the party performing it is independent of the team that builds or runs the system under test. Record the testing party, its relationship to the system owner, the criteria checked, the conclusion, and who accepted it; for an external party record the engagement reference so Procurement's contract can be located from the test file. File the confirmation with the test record so each report can be paired with its independence check. The signed confirmations for the period are the evidence.

evidenceHint.en: Signed tester independence confirmation for each test performed in the period, naming the testing party, its relationship to the system owner, the criteria checked and the acceptor

title.en: Track every finding raised by a test from prioritisation through to remediation

description.en: Enter each finding a test produces into the remediation tracker with the test it came from, the system affected, the priority assigned under the programme's prioritisation rules, the named owner, the agreed remediation and its current state. Keep the state current as the work lands, and record the verification that closed each finding rather than closing it on the owner's assertion. The tracker export for the period, showing open and closed findings with their priority and owner, is the artifact attached.

evidenceHint.en: Remediation tracker export for the period: each test finding with its source test, affected system, priority, owner, remediation state and the verification that closed it

title.en: Verify the programme's coverage of critical ICT systems and record the systems not yet tested

description.en: Compare the tests actually performed against the scope register, to see whether coverage of critical systems is being achieved across the cycle rather than only planned. Mark every critical system as tested, scheduled or not reached, and for each not reached record the cause and what changes in the plan. Where a system was tested but its findings remain open past the date agreed in the tracker, record that too — coverage without remediation leaves the risk exactly where the test found it. Attach the coverage review with its conclusions.

evidenceHint.en: Programme coverage review: every critical system marked tested, scheduled or not reached for the cycle, with the cause and plan change per gap and the findings still open past their agreed date

title: Testing of ICT tools and systems

title.en: Map each ICT system and tool to the test types it must undergo

description.en: Build the matrix that says what kind of testing each system gets — vulnerability assessment, scan, gap analysis, penetration test, scenario-based test — and which combination applies where. Mark the critical ICT systems, which are the ones to be tested at least yearly, and record for each assigned test what it needs in order to run: environment, access, data, and the owner who provides them. A test with no named prerequisite owner is the one that slips. Attach the completed matrix.

evidenceHint.en: Test-type matrix: every ICT system and tool with its critical marking, the test types assigned to it, the prerequisites each test needs and the system owner who provides them

text.en: List every ICT system and tool, marking those identified as critical.
Assign the applicable test types to each system across the range in use.
Record the environment, access and data each assigned test needs to run.
Name the system owner who provides access and prerequisites for each test.

title.en: Schedule at least one test within the year for every critical ICT system in the matrix

description.en: Produce a dated schedule that places at least one test on every critical ICT system within the year, drawing its test type from the matrix, and places the remaining systems according to what the matrix assigns them. Record for each entry the test type, the planned date, the party performing it, and the window agreed with the system owner. Where a critical system cannot be tested within the year, record the obstacle and the interim measure against that entry rather than leaving the slot empty and the gap unstated. Attach the schedule.

evidenceHint.en: Dated test schedule showing at least one test within the year for every critical ICT system, with the test type drawn from the matrix, the performing party, the agreed window, and any obstacle recorded

title.en: Test each scheduled system with a vulnerability assessment or scan and file the resulting report

description.en: Run the vulnerability assessments and scans the schedule calls for, and file the report each produces against the system it covers. A usable report carries the scope actually tested, the date, the tool and its signature or plugin version, whether the scan was authenticated, and the findings with their severity. Where a scheduled scan did not run, or covered less than planned, record that on the report rather than filing nothing — an absent report and a clean one look identical in a folder. The reports for the period are the artifact attached.

evidenceHint.en: Vulnerability assessment and scan reports for the period, each naming the system, the scope actually tested, the date, the tool version, whether it was authenticated, and the findings by severity

title.en: Collect the penetration test and scenario-based test reports for every engagement in the schedule

description.en: For each penetration test and scenario-based test performed, obtain the tester's report and file it against the systems in scope. Check on receipt that it states the scope and the dates tested, the method or scenario used, the findings with their severity, and anything in scope that could not be tested — a report missing those cannot support the conclusion drawn from it, and the time to say so is on receipt. Register the findings so they reach the remediation tracker. Attach the reports for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Penetration test reports and scenario test results for the period, each stating the scope, dates, method or scenario, findings by severity, and any in-scope area that could not be tested

title.en: Verify that every critical ICT system was tested within the last year and record those that were not

description.en: Check the filed reports against the test-type matrix and the schedule to establish that each critical ICT system has been tested within the last year, recording which of the test types the matrix assigns it were performed. Mark every critical system as tested, tested with reduced scope, or not tested, giving the date and report reference for those tested and the cause and remedy for those not. Attach the coverage check: it is what demonstrates the yearly testing of critical systems actually happened, rather than that it was planned.

evidenceHint.en: Annual coverage check listing each critical ICT system as tested, reduced-scope or untested, with the test date, report reference and test types performed for each, and the cause and remedy for every gap

title.en: Record the threat-led penetration testing in-scope determination for the entity

description.en: TLPT applies to identified financial entities, so the first deliverable is the written determination: whether this entity has been identified as in scope, on what basis, who made the determination and when. Where the entity is in scope, record who identified it and the notification that conveyed it if one exists; where it is not, record the basis so the position can be re-taken when the entity's profile changes. Attach the signed determination.

evidenceHint.en: Signed TLPT in-scope determination naming the basis for the conclusion, the decision-maker and the date

title.en: Produce the TLPT scope document covering the critical or important functions and their live production systems

description.en: Write the TLPT scope document this control names as evidence: the critical or important functions the test must cover, the live production systems and services supporting each of them, the threat-led scenarios the test will follow, and the date of the previous test, so the interval against the at-least-every-three-years frequency the article sets is visible before this scope is approved. Derive the function list from the entity's own critical-function register rather than restating the article. Attach the scope document together with its approval.

evidenceHint.en: Approved TLPT scope document listing the critical or important functions, the live production systems in scope and the date of the previous test

text.en: Pull the critical or important functions from the entity's own register.
Map each function to the live production systems and services supporting it.
Set out the threat-led scenarios the test will follow and where they came from.
Record the date of the previous TLPT and the interval this test closes.
Obtain and attach the approval of the scope before any testing begins.

title.en: File the TLPT report for each completed test with its completion date and the functions covered

description.en: When a test completes, file the TLPT report together with the start and completion dates and the list of critical or important functions the test actually exercised — which can differ from the scoped list. Those dates are what lets anyone read the interval between successive tests against the at-least-every-three-years frequency the article sets, so record them on the report itself and not only in a calendar.

evidenceHint.en: TLPT report per completed test, carrying the completion date and the critical or important functions the test exercised

title.en: Obtain the authority attestation for each completed TLPT and file it against the report

description.en: Request and retain the attestation the authorities issue for a completed TLPT, filing it against the report it attests. Record the date the attestation was requested and the date it was received; where one is outstanding, keep the request open rather than closing the test out. This artifact is what shows an external party accepted the exercise as a TLPT, not merely that a test happened.

evidenceHint.en: Attestation by authorities for each completed TLPT, filed with its report and carrying the request and receipt dates

title.en: Track every TLPT finding to closure in the TLPT remediation plan

description.en: Open the remediation plan from the report's findings: one row per finding, carrying the affected function, the owner, the remediation agreed and its current status. Close a row only against evidence that the fix landed, and carry any finding still open into the scope of the next test. Attach the remediation plan showing the status of every finding.

evidenceHint.en: TLPT remediation plan showing each finding, its owner, the remediation agreed and its closure status

title.en: Set out the suitability, independence, certification and indemnity criteria a TLPT tester must meet

description.en: Write the criteria set that every prospective threat-led penetration testing provider is assessed against, so an engagement decision is decidable rather than a judgement made under time pressure. Cover the suitability and reputation the entity requires, the independence it requires from the teams that build, run and defend the systems inside a TLPT scope, the professional-ethics standard or code of conduct the tester adheres to, the certification or accreditation held, and the professional indemnity cover in force. For each criterion record what would count as meeting it, so two assessors applying the set reach the same answer. Attach the criteria set with its version and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: The TLPT tester criteria set, versioned and dated: each suitability, reputation, independence, professional-ethics, certification or accreditation and indemnity criterion with what counts as meeting it

text.en: Record the suitability and reputation criteria a prospective TLPT tester has to meet.
State the independence required from the teams that build, run and defend in-scope systems.
Record the professional-ethics standard and the certification or accreditation expected.
Record the professional indemnity cover the entity requires to be in force.
For each criterion, state the bar an assessor applies to decide it is met.

title.en: Build the due-diligence evidence request that maps each tester criterion to the document proving it

description.en: Turn the criteria set into the pack that goes to a prospective TLPT tester. For each criterion name the document that would prove it — the certification or accreditation certificate, the professional indemnity policy or certificate of cover, the statement of the code of conduct or ethical framework adhered to, and the references or engagement history supporting reputation — and state what the assessor checks on each: that it names the tester being engaged, that it is current, and that it covers the work in question. Record who assesses the returned pack and where the completed record is filed against the engagement. Attach the issued request with its version.

evidenceHint.en: The tester due-diligence evidence request, versioned, mapping every criterion to the document that proves it, what the assessor checks on each, and where the completed record is filed

text.en: Name the document that proves each criterion in the tester criteria set.
State what the assessor checks on each document received back.
Record who assesses the returned pack and where the record is filed.
Record how a criterion answered only in part is to be written down.

title.en: Complete a due-diligence record for every tester engaged on a TLPT and file it with the engagement

description.en: For each TLPT tester engaged in the period, run the evidence request, record the assessment against each criterion, note the documents received and their dates, and record the conclusion reached and who reached it. Where a criterion is met only in part, or the document supplied does not cover the work being engaged, record that against the criterion rather than folding it into the overall conclusion — a partial answer absorbed into a pass is the one nobody can find afterwards. File the completed record against the engagement so the tester file can be reached from the TLPT report. The due-diligence records for the period are the evidence attached.

evidenceHint.en: Tester due-diligence records for the period: per tester the assessment against each criterion, the documents received with their dates, any criterion met only in part, and the conclusion with who reached it

title.en: Assess each TLPT tester's independence from the teams and systems inside the test scope

description.en: Independence is specific to what is being tested, so it is assessed against the scope of the engagement rather than settled once for the tester. For each TLPT engagement record the testing provider and the individuals proposed, the relationship each has to the teams that build, run or defend the systems in the TLPT scope — prior engagements on those systems, group ownership, and any advisory work — the criteria applied from the criteria set, the conclusion reached, and who reached it. Where a relationship exists and the engagement proceeds anyway, record the reasoning and any restriction placed on the tester, so the decision is legible later. Attach the independence assessment for each engagement.

evidenceHint.en: Independence assessment per TLPT engagement: the testing provider and proposed individuals, their relationships to the in-scope teams and systems, the criteria applied, the conclusion, who reached it, and any restriction imposed

text.en: List the testing provider and the individuals proposed for the engagement.
Record each one's relationship to the teams that build, run or defend in-scope systems.
Apply the independence criteria and record the conclusion and who reached it.
Where a relationship exists, record the reasoning and any restriction placed on the tester.

title.en: File the certification or accreditation and the professional indemnity cover held by each TLPT tester

description.en: Keep the documents themselves, not a note that somebody saw them. For each engaged tester file the certification or accreditation document naming the body that issued it and the period it runs for, and the professional indemnity evidence naming the insurer, the cover provided and the period it runs for. On filing, check that each names the tester actually engaged rather than a parent or an affiliate, and record whether its period spans the dates of the test so any gap is visible on the file rather than reconstructed later. Where a document lapses while an engagement is running, note that against the file so it is chased. The filed certificates and cover evidence for the period are the artifact attached.

evidenceHint.en: Certification or accreditation documents and professional indemnity evidence on file per TLPT tester, each naming the tester engaged, its issuing body or insurer, and its period recorded against the test dates

title.en: Re-check that each TLPT run in the period was performed by a tester with a complete and current file

description.en: Take the TLPTs performed in the period and pair each with its tester file. For every one, confirm that a due-diligence record, an independence assessment and the certification and indemnity evidence are all present, that each was made against the criteria set in force at the time, and that nothing on file had lapsed before the test finished. Mark each engagement complete or deficient, and for every deficiency record the cause — a document never chased, an independence assessment made against a different scope, a criterion the set does not in fact make decidable — and the correction it calls for. Attach the completed check with the engagement list it was made from.

evidenceHint.en: Tester file check for the period: each TLPT engagement marked complete or deficient against its due-diligence, independence and certification and indemnity records, with the cause and correction for every deficiency

text.en: List the TLPT engagements performed in the period and pair each with its tester file.
Confirm the due-diligence, independence and certification and indemnity records are present.
Check each was made against the criteria set in force at the time of the engagement.
Record the cause and correction for every engagement marked deficient.

title: ICT third-party risk strategy and Register of Information

title.en: Compile the Register of Information covering every contractual arrangement for the use of ICT services

description.en: Build the register this article requires: one row per contractual arrangement for the use of ICT services, whatever its size or label — cloud service, software subscription, managed service, intra-group arrangement. For each, record the provider, the ICT service supplied, the business function it supports, whether that function is critical or important, the contract dates and the internal owner. Source the population from procurement and finance records rather than from team recall, so an arrangement nobody sponsors still appears. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of Information listing every ICT service contractual arrangement with its provider, the service supplied, the function supported and the contract dates

text.en: Pull the supplier population from procurement and finance records, not team recall.
Record the ICT service supplied and the function it supports for each arrangement.
Flag the arrangements that support a critical or important function.
Record the contract start, renewal and end dates on every row.
Name the internal owner accountable for each arrangement.

title.en: Adopt the ICT third-party risk strategy, including the multi-vendor position

description.en: Take the ICT third-party risk strategy through the entity's own approval route and record who adopted it and when — the article requires the strategy, not a particular approver. It should state how ICT third-party risk is managed as part of the wider ICT risk framework, the entity's position on using more than one vendor for the same ICT service, and the conditions under which an ICT service supporting a critical or important function may be placed with a provider at all. Attach the adopted strategy together with the approval record.

evidenceHint.en: Adopted ICT third-party risk strategy and multi-vendor strategy, with the approval record naming the date and the approver

title.en: Write an exit plan for each ICT service supporting a critical or important function

description.en: For every arrangement flagged critical or important in the Register of Information, produce an exit plan: the conditions that would trigger exit, the steps to move or repatriate the service, the data return and deletion route, any transitional support available under the contract, and the internal owner of the plan. A plan naming no owner and no steps is a statement of intent, not an exit plan. Attach one plan per critical arrangement.

evidenceHint.en: Exit plan per critical or important ICT service, naming the exit triggers, the transition steps, the data return route and the plan owner

title.en: Record the pre-contract ICT risk assessment for each new or renewed ICT arrangement

description.en: Before an ICT contractual arrangement is entered or renewed, complete and file the risk assessment this article expects: the ICT service, the function it supports, the risks identified, the mitigations relied on, and the decision to proceed with the name of whoever took it. Where an assessment is not performed because the arrangement is judged out of scope, record that judgement in the same place — an absent assessment and a considered exclusion must be told apart. Attach the period's assessments.

evidenceHint.en: Pre-contract ICT risk assessments for the period, one per new or renewed arrangement, each carrying the decision to proceed and its author

title.en: Update the Register of Information whenever an ICT arrangement is signed, changed or ended

description.en: Wire register maintenance into the contract lifecycle so the register stays current between reviews: a new signature adds a row, an amendment updates it, a termination closes it with the end date and the exit route taken. Keep the change log alongside so a reader can see when each row last moved and who moved it. Attach the change log for the period together with the current register.

evidenceHint.en: Register of Information change log for the period showing each addition, amendment and closure with its date and author

title.en: Reconcile the Register of Information against the ICT contracts actually held

description.en: Compare the register against the contract population held by procurement and the ICT spend recorded by finance. Record arrangements present in one source and missing from the other, decide which record is correct, and correct it. Report the number of rows reconciled alongside the discrepancies found, so the register's completeness is a measured claim rather than an assumed one.

evidenceHint.en: Register of Information reconciliation record listing the discrepancies found against contract and spend records, and how each was resolved

title.en: Group the ICT arrangements supporting critical or important functions by provider

description.en: Before concentration risk can be assessed it has to be visible. Take the arrangements supporting critical or important functions and group them by provider, showing how many functions each provider sits behind and where separate contracts resolve to the same underlying provider. Attach the resulting provider-to-function view — it is the input every assessment below reads.

evidenceHint.en: Provider-to-function view showing, per ICT provider, the critical or important functions it supports and the arrangements behind them

title.en: Set the method used to assess ICT concentration risk before contracting

description.en: Write down how a concentration-risk assessment is performed, so two assessors reach comparable answers: what is examined — existing arrangements already held with the same provider, the provider's own sub-outsourcing chain, and how readily the provider could be substituted — what evidence is requested from the provider, and who signs the assessment off. Attach the method, approved and version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: Approved ICT concentration-risk assessment method naming the factors examined, the evidence requested from providers and the sign-off

title.en: Complete a concentration-risk assessment before entering each critical-function ICT arrangement

description.en: For every contractual arrangement being entered for an ICT service that supports a critical or important function, complete the assessment under the agreed method and file it before signature. Record the concentration identified, the conclusion reached, and who took the decision to proceed on that basis. Attach the assessments completed in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Concentration risk assessment per critical-function ICT arrangement entered in the period, dated ahead of contract signature

title.en: Document the sub-outsourcing chain declared by each provider of a critical or important function

description.en: Ask each provider supporting a critical or important function to declare the sub-contractors it relies on to deliver that service, and record the chain: the sub-contractor and the part of the service it performs. Record refusals and non-answers explicitly — an undeclared chain is a finding, not an empty field. Attach the sub-outsourcing analysis.

evidenceHint.en: Sub-outsourcing risk analysis recording, per critical provider, the declared sub-contractors and the part of the service each one performs

title.en: Reassess how easily each critical-function ICT provider could be substituted

description.en: For each provider supporting a critical or important function, record what substitution would actually take: whether an alternative provider exists for the same service, what would have to be migrated or rebuilt, and what makes the provider hard to replace where that is the conclusion. Feed anything judged hard to substitute back into exit and contingency planning. Attach the substitutability analysis.

evidenceHint.en: Substitutability analysis stating, per critical-function provider, whether an alternative exists and what substitution would require

title: Key contractual provisions for ICT services

title.en: Turn the mandatory ICT contract provisions into a clause checklist

description.en: List the provisions this article requires an ICT service contract to carry — the service description, the locations where the service is provided and data is processed, data protection commitments, access, inspection and audit rights, termination rights, exit support, and assistance during ICT incidents — and turn each into a checklist line a reviewer can mark present or absent against a draft contract. Attach the checklist, version-marked.

evidenceHint.en: ICT contract clause checklist carrying one line per mandatory provision, version-marked

text.en: Give each mandatory provision the article names its own checklist line.
Write every line so it can be marked present or absent against a draft.
Record where in a contract each provision is normally found.
Name the reviewer who marks the checklist for a given contract.
Version-mark the checklist and publish it to procurement and legal.

title.en: Rewrite the standard ICT contract template so every mandatory provision has its own clause

description.en: Update the standard contractual template used for ICT services so each line of the clause checklist maps to a numbered clause: service description, service and data locations, data protection, access, inspection and audit rights, termination rights, exit support, and assistance during ICT incidents. Keep a clause-to-checklist mapping beside the template so a reviewer can see at a glance which clause satisfies which requirement. Attach the template and the mapping.

evidenceHint.en: Standard ICT contractual template with the clause-to-checklist mapping showing which clause carries each mandatory provision

title.en: Complete the clause checklist for every ICT contract signed or renewed and file it with the executed contract

description.en: Make the checklist part of signature. For each ICT contract entered or renewed, mark every provision present, absent or amended, record where a departure from the standard template was accepted and who accepted it, and file the completed checklist with the executed contract. A contract signed without its checklist is the gap this task closes. Attach the checklists completed in the period.

evidenceHint.en: Completed clause checklist filed with each ICT contract signed or renewed in the period, showing any accepted departures and their approver

title.en: Record the access, inspection and audit rights each ICT contract secures in a single register

description.en: Build and keep the audit and access-rights register: one row per ICT contract, naming the access, inspection and audit rights secured, any notice or conditions attached to exercising them, and the service levels and termination rights agreed. This is what turns a right buried in a signed PDF into something an assessor or an auditor can find on request. Attach the register.

evidenceHint.en: Audit and access-rights register listing, per ICT contract, the access and audit rights secured and the conditions on exercising them

title.en: Re-check ICT contracts predating the clause checklist and log the provisions they lack

description.en: Run the checklist across the ICT contracts that were signed before it existed and are still in force. Record, per contract, which mandatory provisions are missing, the route to fixing it — amendment, renegotiation at renewal, or replacement — and the owner of that route. Attach the gap log; a contract assessed as complete gets a row too, so the population assessed is visible rather than inferred.

evidenceHint.en: Legacy ICT contract gap log naming, per contract, the mandatory provisions missing and the remediation route and owner

title.en: List the ICT third-party providers to be checked against the ESAs' critical-designation list

description.en: A designation attaches to a named legal entity, so the watchlist has to hold the identity a designation could actually be matched against. Draw the providers from the entity's Register of Information and record for each its legal name as contracted, the group parent where the contracting party is a subsidiary, any identifier held for it, the ICT services it supplies, and whether any of those support a critical or important function. Include providers reached through a sub-outsourcing chain where the chain is known, so a designation naming an entity the contract does not name can still be matched. Attach the watchlist.

evidenceHint.en: Designation watchlist: each ICT third-party provider with its contracted legal name, group parent, identifiers, the ICT services supplied and whether any supports a critical or important function

text.en: Draw the provider population from the entity's Register of Information.
Record the contracted legal name, group parent and any identifier held for each provider.
Record the ICT services each supplies and whether any supports a critical or important function.
Add the sub-outsourced entities that are known, so a designation naming one can be matched.

title.en: Establish where the designation list is obtained, who checks it and where the status is recorded

description.en: Set the tracking mechanism up so a designation is noticed rather than discovered. Record the source the ESAs' list of designated critical ICT third-party providers is taken from, the point at which the entity has decided to check it and who performs that check, how a published designation is matched against the watchlist including group and sub-outsourced entities, which field the resulting status is written into against the provider, and who is told when a provider's status changes. Where the entity has set no check point yet, setting one is part of this task. Attach the tracking arrangement with its version and issue date.

evidenceHint.en: The designation tracking arrangement, versioned and dated: the list source, the entity's chosen check point and named checker, the matching rule, the status field and the notification route on a change

text.en: Record the source the ESAs' designation list is obtained from.
Set the point at which the entity checks it and name who performs the check.
Write the rule for matching a published designation against the watchlist.
Name the field the status is recorded in and who is told when it changes.

title.en: Add the designation trigger to contingency and exit planning for ICT third-party providers

description.en: Amend the contingency and exit planning procedure so that a provider being designated critical is one of the events that causes its plans to be revisited, rather than a status noted in a register and acted on nowhere. Record what is reconsidered when the trigger fires — the exit plan for the services that provider supplies, the contingency arrangements relied on if it becomes unavailable, and what the provider's subjection to the Union Oversight Framework changes, if anything, in how the entity manages it — who does that work, and where the revised plans are filed. Attach the amended procedure section showing the trigger.

evidenceHint.en: The amended contingency and exit planning procedure showing designation as a trigger, what is reconsidered when it fires, who does the work and where the revised plans are filed

title.en: Record each designation-status check against the watchlist with its date and outcome

description.en: Each time the check is performed, write it down: the date, who performed it, the version or date of the list consulted, and the outcome for every provider on the watchlist — designated, not designated, or matched through a group or sub-outsourced entity with the reasoning for that match. A check that found no change is recorded in the same detail as one that found a designation, because otherwise it is indistinguishable from a check that never ran. Where a provider could not be matched with confidence, record it as unresolved together with what would settle it. The identification records for the period are the artifact attached.

evidenceHint.en: Critical-provider identification records for the period: each check with its date, the person who performed it, the list version consulted, and the outcome per provider including any unresolved match

title.en: Complete an oversight-framework impact assessment for every provider designated critical

description.en: When a provider on the watchlist is designated, record what that designation means for the entity's own management of it. Cover the ICT services that provider supplies and the functions they support, what the entity concludes changes because the provider is subject to the Union Oversight Framework and what does not, what will be done differently in monitoring, contingency and exit planning as a result, and — where the conclusion is that nothing changes — the reasoning behind it. Record who made the assessment and when. Attach the assessment for each designated provider.

evidenceHint.en: Oversight-framework impact assessment per designated provider: the services and functions affected, what the designation changes and what it does not with the reasoning, the resulting actions, the assessor and the date

text.en: List the ICT services the designated provider supplies and the functions they support.
Record what the entity concludes the designation changes, and what it leaves unchanged.
Record the reasoning wherever the conclusion is that nothing changes.
Name the actions that follow in monitoring, contingency and exit planning.

title.en: Reconcile the designation watchlist against the Register of Information and close what the checks left open

description.en: Compare the watchlist against the Register of Information to find ICT third-party providers under contract that the watchlist does not carry, and watchlist entries whose contracts have ended. Then take the period's identification records and confirm that every provider found to be designated has an impact assessment and the revised contingency and exit plans the trigger calls for, and that every match left unresolved was settled. Record each gap with its cause — a provider added to the register after the watchlist was built, an unresolved match nobody returned to, an assessment raised but never filed — and the correction it calls for. Attach the reconciliation with the register export it was made from.

evidenceHint.en: Watchlist reconciliation for the period: providers in the Register of Information but absent from the watchlist and the reverse, each designated provider's assessment and revised-plan status, the unresolved matches, with the cause and correction per gap

text.en: Compare the watchlist against the Register of Information in both directions.
Confirm each designated provider has an impact assessment and revised plans on file.
Check that every match left unresolved by a period check was settled.
Record the cause and the correction for each gap the reconciliation finds.

title.en: Record which trusted cyber-threat communities the entity takes part in, and the decision to join each

description.en: Information sharing under this article is something a financial entity may do, not must, so the record starts with the decision. For each trusted community the entity participates in — a sector information-sharing community, a national CERT arrangement, a bilateral one — record the decision to join, who took it, the date, and the membership status today. Include communities considered and declined, so a later reader can see the choice was made rather than missed. Attach the membership records.

evidenceHint.en: Membership records naming each cyber-threat community joined, the decision and decision-maker behind it, and its current status

title.en: Sign the information-sharing arrangement setting what may be exchanged and with whom

description.en: Put the arrangement in writing before any intelligence moves: the parties to it, the categories of cyber threat information and intelligence that may be exchanged, the permitted uses and onward-disclosure limits, and the confidentiality terms. This article makes protection of confidentiality a condition of sharing, so an undocumented understanding between analysts is not an arrangement. Attach the signed arrangement for each community.

evidenceHint.en: Signed information-sharing arrangement per community, stating the parties, the information categories exchanged and the confidentiality terms

title.en: Write the pre-disclosure handling rules that keep shared intelligence free of personal and competition-sensitive data

description.en: Turn the arrangement's protections into rules an analyst can apply before pressing send: what must be removed or masked — personal data, customer identifiers, pricing and other competition-sensitive detail — what may be shared as it stands, the confidentiality marking the arrangement requires, and who approves a disclosure that falls outside the rules. Legal/DPO owns the data-protection position; Security engineering applies it. Attach the handling rules.

evidenceHint.en: Data protection safeguards document setting the pre-disclosure handling rules for shared cyber threat information

title.en: Log every cyber-threat disclosure made to a community with the pre-release check applied

description.en: Keep one row per outbound disclosure: the date, the community it went to, a summary of what was shared, who released it, and confirmation that the pre-disclosure handling rules were applied. Where an exception was approved, name the approver in the same row. This log is what shows the safeguards operate rather than merely exist. Attach the log for the period.

evidenceHint.en: Outbound cyber-threat sharing log for the period, one row per disclosure with the handling check and the releaser recorded

title.en: File the notification of participation made to the competent authority where it is required

description.en: Where participation in an information-sharing arrangement has to be notified to the competent authority, record the notification as submitted, its date, the arrangement it covers and any acknowledgement received. Where notification is judged not to be required for a given arrangement, record that judgement and its basis in the same place, so a silence can be told apart from an omission.

evidenceHint.en: Notification of participation as submitted to the competent authority with its date and any acknowledgement, or the recorded basis for not notifying

title.en: Re-read the period's sharing log against the handling rules and record any disclosure that fell outside them

description.en: Walk the outbound sharing log entry by entry against the pre-disclosure handling rules and the terms of the arrangement: was the recipient a party to it, was the release approved by whoever the rules name, and was anything shared that the rules exclude. Record the findings, the correction taken and any change to the rules that followed. Attach the review, including a nil-finding result.

evidenceHint.en: Sharing-log review record listing the entries checked, any disclosure that fell outside the handling rules and the correction taken
